statement.outputFormat: Print YES if the list contains a cycle; otherwise print NO.
constraints: pos is -1 or a valid index from 0 through n−1; pos must be -1 when n=0.

hints: Repeated values do not imply a cycle; repeated node identities do.

statement.description: Find the length of the longest contiguous part of a string whose characters are all different. Character comparisons are case-sensitive.
statement.inputFormat: First token: n, the string length. If n is positive, the next token is the string; if n is zero, there is no string token.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum length; an empty string has answer 0.
constraints: The string contains only ASCII letters and digits.
statement.approach: Track the most recent index of each character. When a character repeats inside the current window, move the left boundary just past its previous occurrence. Never move the boundary backward.
statement.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed ASCII alphabet.
hints: A substring must be contiguous.
Use max(left, previousIndex + 1) when a character repeats.

from heapq import heappush, heappop

 left=max(left,last.get(ch,-1)+1);last[ch]=right;best=max(best,right-left+1)
print(best)

statement.description: Find every distinct triple of values that sums to zero using three different array positions. Repeated input values are allowed, but each value triple must be printed only once.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n integers.
statement.outputFormat: Print the number of triples, then one triple per line. Values within each triple must be in nondecreasing order. Triple lines may appear in any order. Print only 0 when no triple exists.
constraints: The input has at most 1000 distinct zero-sum triples.
statement.approach: Sort the array. Fix each distinct first value and scan the remaining suffix with two pointers. Move the lower pointer when the sum is negative and the upper pointer when it is positive; after a match, skip repeated endpoint values.
statement.complexity: O(n^2) time, O(n+t) space including sorted input and t output triples.
hints: Three copies of 0 yield one triple, but two copies do not.
Skip duplicates both for the fixed value and after recording a pair.

python.solution:
import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();a=sorted(ni() for _ in range(n));out=[]
for i in range(n-2):
 if i and a[i]==a[i-1]:continue
 l=i+1;r=n-1
 while l<r:
  total=a[i]+a[l]+a[r]
  if total<0:l+=1
  elif total>0:r-=1
  else:
   out.append((a[i],a[l],a[r]));x,y=a[l],a[r]
   while l<r and a[l]==x:l+=1
   while l<r and a[r]==y:r-=1
print(len(out))
for row in out:print(*row)

statement.description: Vertical lines stand at integer positions 0 through n-1. A pair of lines holds an area equal to their distance multiplied by the shorter height. Find the largest possible area.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n nonnegative heights.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum area as a 64-bit integer.
statement.approach: Start at the outermost lines. Record their area, then move the pointer at the shorter line: keeping that line while reducing the width cannot improve the area.
statement.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) space for input and O(1) auxiliary space.
hints: The shorter line limits the water height.
Multiply using 64-bit arithmetic before comparing areas.

statement.description: For each array position, compute the product of every input value except the value at that position. Solve the problem without division, including when the input contains zeros.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n integers.
statement.outputFormat: Print n products in the original position order, separated by spaces.
constraints: Every contiguous product and every requested output fits in a signed 64-bit integer.
statement.approach: Store the product strictly to the left of each position. Scan backward with a running product strictly to the right and multiply it into the stored answer.
statement.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) output space and O(1) auxiliary space beyond input/output.
hints: One zero and two zeros lead to different answers.
Use 1 as the product of an empty prefix or suffix.

statement.description: Return the k distinct values that occur most often in an array. The input guarantees that the selected set is unique: if any values are excluded, every selected value occurs more often than every excluded value.
statement.inputFormat: n and k, followed by n integers.
statement.outputFormat: Print the k selected values in any order, with no count prefix.
constraints: 1 <= k <= min(2000, number of distinct values)
No frequency tie crosses the selection boundary.
statement.approach: Count each value with a hash map, sort the distinct values by decreasing count, and return the first k. A value tie-breaker makes the reference output reproducible but is not required.
statement.complexity: O(n+d log d) expected time, O(d) space, where d is the number of distinct values.
hints: Rank distinct values, not individual occurrences.
Equal frequencies within the selected set are permitted.

statement.description: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values present anywhere in the array. Their positions do not have to be adjacent or in order, and duplicates do not extend a run.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n integers. n may be zero.
statement.outputFormat: Print the longest run length; print 0 for an empty array.
statement.approach: Put the values in a set. Only start counting at a value whose predecessor is absent, then advance through its consecutive successors. Each distinct value belongs to just one counted run.
statement.complexity: O(n) expected time, O(n) space.
hints: Starting a scan at every value can repeat the same work.
A run starts at x exactly when x-1 is absent.

for x in values:
 if x-1 not in values:
  end=x
  while end in values:end+=1

statement.description: An array was strictly increasing, then rotated by moving a prefix to its end, possibly moving no elements. Find the position of a target value in the rotated array.
statement.inputFormat: n and target, followed by n distinct integers.
statement.outputFormat: Print the zero-based target index, or -1 if the target is absent.
constraints: The array is a rotation of a strictly increasing array.
statement.approach: At every binary-search step, at least one half is sorted. Check whether the target lies inside that sorted half and retain the appropriate half.
statement.complexity: O(log n) search time after O(n) input reading; O(1) auxiliary space beyond the input.
hints: Identify a sorted half before discarding indices.
The target may lie on either side of the rotation pivot.

python.solution:
import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();target=ni();a=[ni() for _ in range(n)];l=0;r=n-1;answer=-1
while l<=r:
 m=(l+r)//2
 if a[m]==target:answer=m;break
 if a[l]<=a[m]:
  if a[l]<=target<a[m]:r=m-1
  else:l=m+1
 else:
  if a[m]<target<=a[r]:l=m+1
  else:r=m-1
print(answer)

When a[mid] <= a[right], use right = mid rather than mid - 1.

statement.description: Combine overlapping closed intervals into disjoint closed intervals with the same covered points. Intervals that touch at an endpoint overlap. Input intervals may be unsorted, nested or repeated.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n lines containing start and end.
statement.outputFormat: Print the merged interval count, then one start end pair per line in increasing start order.
statement.approach: Sort by start. If the next interval starts at or before the current end, extend that end; otherwise begin a new result interval.
statement.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space including the result.
hints: Use <= when deciding whether closed intervals overlap.
An interval contained in the current interval must not reduce its end.

statement.description: Insert one closed interval into an already sorted collection of nonoverlapping closed intervals. Merge everything that overlaps, including intervals that meet at an endpoint.
statement.inputFormat: n, then n start end pairs in increasing start order, then the new interval start end pair.
statement.outputFormat: Print the resulting interval count, then one start end pair per line in increasing start order.
constraints: For existing neighbors, previous end < next start.
statement.approach: Copy intervals strictly before the new interval. Expand the new interval across every overlapping interval, append the expansion, then copy all remaining intervals.
statement.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) space including the result.
hints: The inserted interval can absorb several existing intervals.
Distinguish intervals strictly before, overlapping, and strictly after.

import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();a=[(ni(),ni()) for _ in range(n)];left=ni();right=ni();i=0;out=[]
while i<n and a[i][1]<left:out.append(a[i]);i+=1
while i<n and a[i][0]<=right:left=min(left,a[i][0]);right=max(right,a[i][1]);i+=1
out.append((left,right));out.extend(a[i:]);print(len(out))
for row in out:print(*row)

statement.complexity: O(rows*columns) time and space.
hints: All initial rotten oranges act at time zero.
Empty cells block transmission; they do not become rotten.

import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
m=ni();tokens=[next(data) for _ in range(m)];values=[0]*m;left=[-1]*m;right=[-1]*m;root=-1 if not m or tokens[0]=='null' else 0;build=deque()
if root!=-1:values[0]=int(tokens[0]);build.append(0)
position=1
while build and position<m:
 parent=build.popleft()
 for side in range(2):
  if position==m:break
  if tokens[position]!='null':
   values[position]=int(tokens[position])
   if side==0:left[parent]=position
   else:right[parent]=position
   build.append(position)
  position+=1
stack=[];node=root;previous=None;valid=True
while node!=-1 or stack:
 while node!=-1:stack.append(node);node=left[node]
 node=stack.pop()
 if previous is not None and values[node]<=previous:valid=False;break
 previous=values[node];node=right[node]
print('YES' if valid else 'NO')

statement.inputFormat: First token: m, the number of tree tokens. Then m compact level-order tokens, each an integer or null. The encoding is valid and contains no tokens after all child slots are exhausted. After the m tree tokens, read k.
statement.outputFormat: Print the kth smallest value.
constraints: The encoded tree is nonempty and is a valid strict binary search tree.
statement.approach: Perform an iterative inorder traversal, which visits BST values in increasing order. Count visits and stop when the kth value is reached.

hints: Inorder traversal visits the left subtree, node, then right subtree.

 if k==0:print(values[node]);break

statement.description: Two linked lists store nonnegative decimal integers, one digit per node, with the least significant digit first. Add the integers and return the sum in the same digit order. The input adapter supplies list digits in head-to-tail order.
statement.inputFormat: n and m, followed by n digits of the first list, then m digits of the second list. The final digit of each input list is nonzero unless that list consists of the single digit 0.
statement.outputFormat: Print the number of digits in the sum, then its digits from least significant to most significant on the next line. Print zero as one digit 0.
statement.approach: Build the two linked lists and walk their heads together. Add the current digits and carry, append sum modulo 10 to the result, and carry sum divided by 10. Continue while either list or a final carry remains.
statement.complexity: O(n+m) time, O(n+m) storage including adapted input lists and output.
hints: Do not convert the entire lists to a fixed-width integer.
The result can have one more digit than either input.

python.solution:
import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();m=ni()
class Node:
 def __init__(self,digit):self.digit=digit;self.next=None
def read_list(count):
 dummy=Node(0);tail=dummy
 for _ in range(count):tail.next=Node(ni());tail=tail.next
 return dummy.next
a=read_list(n);b=read_list(m);carry=0;out=[]
while a is not None or b is not None or carry:
 total=carry
 if a is not None:total+=a.digit;a=a.next
 if b is not None:total+=b.digit;b=b.next
 out.append(total%10);carry=total//10
print(len(out));print(*out)

statement.description: A skyline consists of adjacent unit-width bars. After rain, water stays in gaps bounded by taller bars. Find the total number of unit squares of trapped water; water beyond either end drains away.
statement.inputFormat: An integer n, followed by n nonnegative bar heights. When n is 0 there are no heights.
statement.outputFormat: Print the total trapped water as an integer.
constraints: 0 ≤ height ≤ 1000000000; the answer may require 64-bit arithmetic.
statement.approach: Move inward from both ends while maintaining the largest height seen on each side. Finalize the side with the smaller current boundary, because the opposite boundary is already high enough to contain its water.
statement.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space beyond the input array.
hints: Water above a bar is limited by the smaller of its left and right maximum heights.
Finalize one side at a time; use a 64-bit total.

statement.description: You receive k singly linked lists, each already sorted in nondecreasing order. Merge their nodes into one sorted list, preserving every occurrence of every value. A list, or the entire collection, may be empty.
statement.inputFormat: First k. For each list: its length followed by that many integer node values, in list order. Whitespace and line breaks are interchangeable.
statement.outputFormat: Print the merged values separated by spaces. Print an empty line when there are no nodes.
constraints: Each input list is sorted in nondecreasing order.
statement.approach: Put each nonempty list head into a min-heap. Repeatedly remove the smallest node, attach it to the output, and add its original successor to the heap. There is at most one heap entry per input list.
statement.complexity: O(k + N log(k+1)) time and O(k) auxiliary space beyond the linked nodes and printed output.
hints: The next output node must be one of the current list heads.
After removing a heap node, offer its successor; retain duplicate values.

import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
class Node:
    def __init__(self,v):self.v=v;self.next=None
k=ni();heap=[]
for i in range(k):
    n=ni();head=tail=None
    for _ in range(n):
        p=Node(ni())
        if head is None:head=p
        else:tail.next=p
        tail=p
    if head is not None:heappush(heap,(head.v,i,head))
dummy=Node(0);tail=dummy
while heap:
    _,i,p=heappop(heap)
    if p.next is not None:heappush(heap,(p.next.v,i,p.next))
    tail.next=p;tail=p
tail.next=None;out=[];p=dummy.next
while p is not None:out.append(str(p.v));p=p.next
print(' '.join(out))

statement.description: Reverse a singly linked list in consecutive groups of exactly k nodes. Any final group with fewer than k nodes keeps its original order. Solve by changing links rather than swapping node values.
statement.inputFormat: n and k, followed by n integer node values in list order.
statement.outputFormat: Print the values after the group reversals, separated by spaces; use an empty line for an empty list.
statement.approach: Use a dummy head and locate the kth node after the previous group. If it exists, reverse exactly that segment toward the following node, reconnect the segment, and advance. Stop when a complete group is unavailable.
statement.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space beyond the linked nodes and printed output.
hints: Check that a full group exists before changing any links.
The old first node becomes the last node of a reversed group.

n=ni();k=ni();dummy=Node(0);tail=dummy
for _ in range(n):tail.next=Node(ni());tail=tail.next
before=dummy
while True:

        if kth is None:break
    if kth is None:break
    after=kth.next;old_first=before.next;prev=after;cur=old_first

statement.description: Find the shortest contiguous substring of s containing every character of t with at least its required multiplicity. Matching is case-sensitive. If several shortest windows exist, choose the one that starts earliest. An empty target requires the empty window.
statement.inputFormat: Two whitespace-separated strings s and t. Each consists of English letters; the single token - represents an empty string.
statement.outputFormat: Print the selected substring. Print EMPTY for an empty target, or NONE if a nonempty target cannot be covered.
constraints: Nonempty strings contain only A–Z and a–z.
statement.approach: Maintain required character counts and a count of still-missing occurrences. Expand the right edge until the window covers t, then shrink from the left while coverage holds. Update the answer only on a strictly shorter window to preserve the earliest tie.
statement.complexity: O(|s|+|t|) time and O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed alphabet.
hints: Repeated characters in t require repeated occurrences in the window.
A negative remaining count means that character is currently present in excess.

import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
s=next(data);t=next(data);s='' if s=='-' else s;t='' if t=='-' else t
if not t:print('EMPTY')
else:
    need=Counter(t);missing=len(t);left=0;best_start=0;best=len(s)+1
    for right,ch in enumerate(s):
        if need[ch]>0:missing-=1
        need[ch]-=1
        while missing==0:
            if right-left+1<best:best=right-left+1;best_start=left
            old=s[left];left+=1;need[old]+=1
            if need[old]>0:missing+=1
    print('NONE' if best>len(s) else s[best_start:best_start+best])

statement.description: A histogram contains adjacent unit-width bars. Choose consecutive bars and a rectangle whose height does not exceed any chosen bar. Find the largest possible rectangle area. An empty histogram has area 0.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n nonnegative bar heights.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum rectangle area as an integer.
statement.approach: Maintain a stack of indices with nondecreasing heights. When a shorter bar arrives, pop taller bars and compute their largest span using the new stack top as the left boundary. A final zero-height sentinel flushes all remaining positive bars.
statement.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
hints: Each bar can be the limiting height of a rectangle.
After a pop, the span ends just before the current bar and begins just after the new stack top.

import sys

from bisect import bisect_left

def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();a=[ni() for _ in range(n)]+[0];stack=[];best=0

    while stack and a[stack[-1]]>a[i]:
        h=a[stack.pop()];left=stack[-1] if stack else -1
        best=max(best,h*(i-left-1))

statement.description: A path in a binary tree follows edges between distinct nodes without revisiting a node. It may start and end anywhere and must contain at least one node. Find the largest sum of node values along any path.
statement.inputFormat: A token count m, followed by m compact level-order tokens. A token is an integer value or null for an absent child. Start with the root, then consume the left and right child tokens for each non-null node in queue order; omitted trailing child tokens are null. The tree is valid and nonempty.
statement.outputFormat: Print the largest path sum as an integer.
statement.approach: Build child indices in breadth-first order, then process nodes in reverse creation order so children are ready before parents. The gain offered to a parent uses at most one child; the best path centered at a node may use both positive child gains.
statement.complexity: O(m) time and O(m) space, with no recursive calls.
hints: Discard a negative child gain when extending a path.
Initialize the global answer below all possible node values so all-negative trees work.

import sys
from collections import deque, Counter

m=ni();tok=[next(data) for _ in range(m)];val=[int(tok[0])];left=[-1];right=[-1];pos=1;p=0
while p<len(val) and pos<m:
    for side in range(2):
        if pos==m:break
        s=tok[pos];pos+=1
        if s!='null':
            child=len(val);val.append(int(s));left.append(-1);right.append(-1)
            if side==0:left[p]=child

    p+=1
gain=[0]*len(val);best=-10**30

    b=max(0,gain[right[p]]) if right[p]>=0 else 0
    best=max(best,val[p]+a+b);gain[p]=val[p]+max(a,b)
print(best)

The empty tree is represented by the single token null in both formats. Integer values must be printed in ordinary decimal notation.
statement.inputFormat: An operation SERIALIZE or DESERIALIZE, then token count m, then m tokens (integer values or null). For SERIALIZE, tokens are compact level order: root first, then left and right children of each non-null node in queue order; omitted trailing children are null. For DESERIALIZE, tokens are a valid complete preorder stream with explicit null children. All inputs describe valid trees.
statement.outputFormat: Print the output token count on the first line and the output tokens separated by spaces on the second line. SERIALIZE outputs complete preorder; DESERIALIZE outputs compact level order with trailing nulls removed, or one null for the empty tree.
constraints: A complete preorder stream for n nodes contains exactly 2n+1 tokens.
statement.approach: For level-order input, attach children using a queue. For preorder input, use a stack of pending left/right child slots so every null fixes an exact missing edge. Serialize with an iterative preorder stack including null entries. To emit level order after deserialization, queue child slots and trim only the trailing nulls.
statement.complexity: O(m) time and O(m) space, using iterative traversals that also handle very deep trees.
hints: A list of only node values cannot distinguish different tree shapes.
Preorder parsing must consume a null token without creating a node.
The two operations have different traversal orders; copying or merely trimming the input is insufficient.

statement.description: Find every dictionary word that can be traced on a rectangular letter board. Consecutive letters must use cells sharing an edge, and a cell cannot be reused within one word. Return each found word once, even if the dictionary repeats it or several board paths spell it.
statement.inputFormat: r and c, followed by r lowercase strings of length c. Then w, followed by w nonempty lowercase dictionary words.
statement.outputFormat: Print all distinct found words separated by whitespace, in any order. If none are found, print an empty line.
constraints: The sum S of dictionary word lengths is at most 20000.
statement.approach: Store dictionary words in a trie. Start a depth-first search at each board cell and follow only trie edges matching adjacent cells. Temporarily mark each visited cell, restore it on return, and clear a terminal word after reporting it to prevent duplicates.
statement.complexity: O(S + r·c·4·3^(L−1)) worst-case time and O(S+L) auxiliary space, where L is the maximum word length (take L=1 for an empty dictionary). Trie pruning often makes the search much smaller.
hints: Share searches for words with a common prefix using a trie.
Restore the board cell after exploring a path.
Finding a shorter word must not stop the search for longer words sharing its prefix.

statement.description: Move a window of exactly k consecutive values from left to right across an array. For each window position, report its largest value.
statement.inputFormat: n and k, followed by n integer array values.
statement.outputFormat: Print the n−k+1 window maxima in left-to-right order.
statement.approach: Maintain a deque of indices whose values decrease from front to back. Remove indices outside the current window and discard smaller or equal values from the back before adding the new index. The front is the maximum.
statement.complexity: O(n) time and O(k) auxiliary space beyond the input and output.
hints: Store indices, since you must know when a candidate expires.
A newer value at least as large makes an older candidate unnecessary.

statement.description: Maintain a growing multiset of integers. ADD x inserts x, including duplicates. MEDIAN asks for the middle value after sorting, or the arithmetic mean of the two middle values when the size is even. Answer every query without sorting the entire stream again.
statement.inputFormat: q, followed by q operations: ADD x or MEDIAN. Every MEDIAN occurs after at least one ADD.
statement.outputFormat: For each MEDIAN, print one line with exactly one decimal digit: .0 for an integer or .5 for a half-integer. Negative halves must retain their sign, such as -0.5.
statement.approach: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap. Rebalance so the lower heap has the same size as the upper heap or one extra item. The median comes from the heap tops. Format twice the median as an integer to avoid floating-point or negative-rounding mistakes.
statement.complexity: O(log q) time per ADD, O(1) per MEDIAN, and O(q) space.
hints: All values in the lower heap must be at most all values in the upper heap.
For an even count, add the two middle values using 64-bit arithmetic.
Format the sign separately from the absolute doubled median.
